description: Cooks every Sunday and keeps making dishes. Studies Japanese on their own, chose a Japanese history elective to understand the culture, watches anime and wants to visit Kyoto. Has three side projects.
tests: When one topic shows up repeatedly across different contexts (self-study, elective class, anime, travel), the topic-level generalization IS allowed. Guards against being so cautious that nothing is promoted

observations.note: The student cooked shakshuka with cumin and a little feta on the morning of 2026-09-06.
The student says they cook every Sunday as a weekly reset, and that chopping vegetables clears their head.
observations.hook: Using repetitive vegetable chopping as a way to clear their head and reset for the week
observations.quote: I cook every Sunday no matter what. It's my reset for the week, chopping vegetables just clears my head.

observations.note: The student usually chooses what to cook on Sunday morning based on what is in the fridge.
observations.hook: Making a choice in the moment using whatever ingredients are available
observations.quote: Usually decide that morning based on whatever's in the fridge.

observations.note: The student made shoyu ramen with chicken from scratch; the broth took seven hours, and they found the tare the hardest part.
observations.quote: Made ramen from scratch yesterday. Took me 7 hours for the broth lol

observations.note: The student has been using Duolingo to learn Japanese for about three months and felt proud when they could read some of the soy sauce bottle label; they clarified that nobody asked them to learn it and they wanted to.
observations.hook: Being able to use a self-chosen skill in an everyday real-world moment
observations.caveat: They could read only some of the label.
observations.quote: Nobody asked me to learn it, I just wanted to.

observations.note: Outside the syllabus question, the student asked how sakoku affected Edo-era eating and whether sushi came from that period. They said they chose the elective to understand the culture behind food and a language they are into.
observations.hook: Understanding culture through the history behind food and language
observations.quote: I picked this elective because I wanted to understand the culture behind the food and the language I'm into.

observations.note: The student found the idea of sushi as fast food amusing.
observations.hook: The surprising contrast of a familiar food being described as fast food
observations.quote: Sushi as fast food is so funny.

observations.note: The student said they want to visit Kyoto someday and are saving for a possible trip next year. They are especially drawn to temple scenes in anime.
observations.topic: Kyoto travel and anime temple scenes
observations.hook: Temple settings as depicted in anime
observations.quote: the temple scenes in anime always get me
